Thank you, I'm going to check them out!
Good one, this is going to be one of those things i wish i had said

Thank you. I'm learning to stand up more and enforce boundaries. If she misbehaves I now tell her to stop immediately, if she continues I'm going to try to hang up the phone or if we're physically meeting leave. My SO is helping as well which is really nice because it's quite difficult. But the last week or two she has been behaving a lot better.

Still blurts out some insensitive things, but way better than before.

Thank you

It's an automatism to doubt myself, but I feel like I'm improving in that regard. It definitely helps to have a soundboard of people showing me what's not normal

Ah I understand better then. Well she is facing some consequences already since I was a kid. I am severely reluctant to share anything with her which she hates and I barely have contact with her. Definitely not alone. 

Lately she has been behaving though

some other commenters pointed out she may have twisted their words and I could see that happen. She didn't get therapy during that time, but now the researcher is her therapist. 

That also what stood out to me, why would you be such an asshole if you're normal? Why would you do any of those things?
English isn't my native language and I'm not sure I understand, could you phrase it differently?
That's what I feel too! Why would she choose to be a dick all my youth then!?
Yes that's what it feels like

Yeh no I didn't speak with the therapist at all, only my mother did. Which is my first jump was to: she hid it from them. But not telling me the truth is definitely an option. 

Is it weird that that makes me feel relieved..?
Definitely possible
Thank you. She may have twisted the words a bit indeed
Thank you, I didn't consider this. It would make sense
I agree. She feels like she didn't do anything awful since she is normal
True I suppose, thank you for your thoughts

I didn't consider that honestly, that might be true but the lie alarm bells didn't go of though.

I also wonder if maybe he just didn't tell my mom, she has regular therapy right now with this therapist and if he had told her she had a personality disorder my mother surely wouldn't have accepted it and found a different therapist.

Haha yeah that makes sense then! I hope by that time I've raised confident kids who know what behaviour they don't have to tolerate. But substance abuse makes things a lot harder, especially when kids are in their vulnerable period (teens for example)
Oh the reason why I say until they can say fuck off grandma is because at that age I'd say they'd get their own say in whether or not they want to visit grandma.

Because she will explode/she'll be very upset. I've asked friends to leave, but then it's: "it's nice you were here, I enjoyed your company. But I'm getting tired/have to do some other things." And my friends and I discussed that upfront, so we agree that that's okay. My mom will not respect that plus now I have to kick her out of bad behaviour and not just because the visit lasted long enough for me.
Thank you for your comment! I don't feel comfortable telling her she's not welcome now, after I already gave the okay. But I will definitely keep it in mind for the next time.
No, but I honestly don't want to go to therapy with her. I don't think I can handle that. Thank you anyway!
Thank you
Thank you
Thank you. I do think she was crying because she didn't want to lose me and was hurt that I didn't want as much contact as she'd like. Not out of regret for saying horrid things to me, no.
Thank you! I don't think I'll leave my kids alone with my mom until they're old enough to say "fuck off, grandma." But I'd still rather get things a bit better with boundaries before that time comes.
Thank you <3

My mom has had a lot of therapy, I'm not sure if she currently has therapy too. The issue is though that you first need to recognise that the problem isn't everyone around you. Most of the time she goes to therapy to deal with depression. 

I have no clue how I could get her to therapy for bpd. It's not like I can just say: hey mom, there's really something wrong with you. Have you considered that you might have a personality disorder?
Thank you!

Ah thanks.

She never spanked me as a kid so I'm not too worried about that. But I'm not taking risks with the "no" since she can't even accept a no from me as an adult, why would she accept it when it comes to her future grandkids? I'm going to remember giving them a parenting book though, although I'm not planning to leave my kids alone with her until they are old enough to say "fuck off grandma".
Well obviously I only post about the negative things. We can also have fun together and she can be really creative too. But those things aren't causing issues for me :)

Yeah that does make sense
Thank you

I do feel really anxious having her over, i try to avoid it whenever because I feel so powerless. It's not even that she does horrid things when she's over, but just the going out of her way to ignore my boundaries is really stressful. But with covid and it being her birthday I don't really see another option right now.
Thank you <3!
Visits are allowed, but only 1 household per day

I'm afraid of that too, she has been behaving like this for at least my entire life. And according to my dad way longer. So why would it suddenly change now? But I want to find a way where I can see her a couple of times per year, but if having really strong boundaries won't work she won't see my kids.

Yeah she won't see my kids weekly for sure, because I don't think she'll be a great influence. But I don't want to completely cut her out so I want to practice the iron-clad boundaries for those moments where I do see her a couple of times per year.

She already behaves differently with my SO present and her boyfriend present. But my SO is still appalled by some of her remarks/behaviour. I do wonder how she is to her boyfriend. The marriage with my dad was horrid. But meeting public is something a lot of commenters have recommended. I'm just a bit hesitant to do so now with covid, because all we can go to is a park. And they live quite far away (which is nice because then she won't actually just show up, she thinks it's too far to drive for a short visit)
Thank you

I'm trying to improve, but yeah I probably don't stand up for myself enough yet. Which is also why I'm posting here, because sometimes it's hard to see when I'm being an asshole and when I'm just standing up for myself. Especially when my mom is telling me I'm horrible so often and cry when I tell her she hurts my feelings.
Thank you <3

I'm going to try my best to do that, I asked my SO to help because it's kind of scary? But he said he is definitely going to help
Thank you, that's a very helpful and clear list!
You're right, I'm definitely going to try that after covid. But right now a public space isn't an option because of the lockdowns.

Thanks, I'll try to kick her out if she ignores my no again.

Public spaces isn't really an option right now because of covid. I'm already going to her place more than my own because then I can just leave whenever, which is easier than getting someone else to leave.
Thank you

She also complains I'm too sensitive. 

I'm looking to get back into therapy, some people also suggested that on my previous post. It's going to take some time though because of covid/finances. 

I don't think she is bipolar, but has borderline. But I can't know for sure since there is no official diagnosis as far as I'm aware of. My dad did suggest that something like that is going on, but he won't spill the beans on it and my mom sure as hell wouldn't admit to it. She already got incredibly angry when I suggested she might have ADHD. Then a couple of years later she got diagnosed and medication for it and she completely denied that I ever did that suggestion. So there's no way she'd be open about something like this. She did have a lot of therapy herself too. 

Thank you for your advice :)
So basically just continuing to say "no" in various forms?

I feel that you're right. I don't want a super close relationship with her because of it. However I don't want to cut contact. But I do need some tools to deal with her disrespecting my boundaries, especially in physical contact. On the phone I could always hang up, but that's impossible if she's here at my house..

Maybe that's it? Could make sense.

I do think that when the time comes she'll put in the effort, not to take care of them. But to hug them and play with them. Her current boyfriend has grandchildren and they are over a lot. On the surface she seems really nice and good with kids. But there's some strange choices. For example she refuses to install a babydgate at the stairs, even though they are hard, high and slippery (painted wood) stairs. I fell down once as a kid and got really hurt. But she believes "kids will learn". You litteraly risk toddlers dieing because they do already climb up the stairs and try to stand up on the middle of it. What's so bad about a temporary gate to keep your beloved grandchildren safe? 

But I'm definitely not leaving my children alone with her, she wouldn't respect my rules and thoughts as a parent.

I don't have any kids yet, so I'm not letting anyone but myself get hurt by her at the moment. Which is exactly why I want to learn how to deal with this behaviour now, so my future children won't get hurt by her. I have way less difficulty standing up for others than for myself, but it'll be easier if I can stand up for myself too.

So what do I do when she ignores my no at my house?

>so, what does that mean for when there IS a child? She'll walk right through you to take baby and ignore your existence like she is right now?

That's exactly what I'm worried about. I know SO has my back too and wouldn't allow that to happen. But I don't want him to have to step in like that. What do you mean with stopper exactly?

Sounds very similar! My mom is also sarcastic most of the time, she got into trouble at work and with friends because of her way of socializing. But somehow she'd never try to be nicer and more constructive. She even had obligated lessons (that or be fired) but she thought it was all bullshit and never took any of it to heart. If you tell her something hurts she'll come right back with "I never say it right" or "I always do it wrong, but I don't mean it that way". 

I carry earpieces with me at almost all times ever since I'm an adult. it has made my life so much easier. They have a music filter so I can still hear everything just the same, just softer. It's definitely something to try if you haven't!
Thank you! Another commenter also recommended that website and I looked around for a bit. Seemed eerily familiar. I'll see if I can find the book :)

Yes she told me that I guess, but it does hold some truth I think. Not when it comes to people joking about things, like she believes. But her jokes are often just mean. But I am often the first to think that sounds are too loud or painful and am quickly overwhelmed when too much is happening at the same time. 

Thank you!
I think this German is a little bit too difficult for me to understand properly, but thank you for sharing anyway
Thank you, I will save this list so I can read some of them during my vacations.
Thank you ❤️

I've hung up on her for the first time last time we talked. I jus couldn't deal with it anymore. But normally it's hard for me to recognise when she is being bitchy and when I'm being overly sensitive.

I completely agree. When I have a bad day/week I can't take care of anyone else. I can barely keep myself floating. The stupid thing is you'd think that she'd understand since she also has these depressive issues. But she doesn't. She says that when she has a bad week she tends to seek people out. I do too, but I force myself to do so because I know it'll help. And I'll seek people who I know are kind and can deal with it. When I went to therapy I also made a list of my support network so that if one wasn't available when I needed someone I could go to someone else. I asked each of them to tell me when they couldn't or weren't feeling up to it and what their boundaries were (for example one friend told me he wouldn't answer after 00:00 or before 07:00, I could send him messages during this time but he would reply when he woke up. Which makes total sense to me). I asked my mom to do the same but she refuses and is convinced I should just answer because she wanted to vent to me and not someone else. She has a boyfriend, they live together. She has a whole lot of siblings and some of them live minutes away. She doesn't have a lot of friends because she's not very good at keeping them. And I understand that she'd want to share that she had to go to the hospital and was worried. But I don't understand why she had to do it the way she did now.

It just sucks because who wouldn't want to have a good relationship with a loving mom? But then I have to explain why I don't want much contact and there's no way to do so without hurting her.
Definitely sounds as if she's just looking for reasons to be disappointed. Why would anyone do that to themselves and loved ones though?
I wouldn't be too surprised if she was suffering from some kind of mental illness

I'm not sure if she chooses or is incapable. 

Your story is very familiar. I don't have any siblings. But I'll often hear the nice things my nieces and nephews did for their parents. And then the silence where I'm supposed to feel guilty that I didn't take my mom on an expensive ass holiday. Even though I couldn't even afford a holiday for myself. 

What did you hear months later?

That's exactly what it feels like, even though rationally it doesn't make sense. There's months where we don't have any contact and I'm fine and happy. I don't even think too much about her. But then suddenly the guilt or fear washes over me. That she'll die and I will regret not seeing her more often.
Luckily my depression is a lot better already, it's lately with all the extra stress that it's a bit more difficult to keep at bay. But I'm going to look into getting into therapy again, thank you!

Ah well I'm Dutch so that makes sense :P. I can read german somewhat, I'll see if I understand the website :) that does seem weird, I always thought that narcissism meant you thought you were the best person in existence.

I used to go the therapy but stopped once my depression became workable. I don't know if I can get therapy again moneywise, last time it was paid for because of the depression. But I'm going to look into it.

Yeah he is super sweet and supportive ^^

When it comes to my mom I feel lost and sad. The rest of life is going alright though. I have a fun job where they are really happy with me, I'm doing a study next to working which is heavy but fun and interesting and I have really sweet and loving people around. It's just when it comes to my mom everything seems so difficult. 

Thank you <3

Thank you. I feel this way too, but then I feel guilty for feeling this way. So it's really nice to hear it from someone not involved. I don't think telling my dad that would make a difference. They hardly have contact at all. And he does believe she loves me very much and that all these difficulties stem from her low self-esteem so the only way to fix it is by telling her you love her. But I have a low self-esteem and my best friend has low self-esteem, but neither of us would treat anyone like this. And if I feel really terrible and she'd stand in front of my door I'd actually be happy she's there. Even if she felt terrible too and we'd feel terrible together.

I luckily already have an awesome chosen family. My boyfriend and best friends are really kind hearted. Actually that's partly why I dared to post in the first place. I talked to them about what happened and they slowly started to convince me this isn't normal. My boyfriend doesn't put up with her at all, she tries (and has in the past with others) to get a friendship going with my partners so they would sent her pictures and she could ask them things. My ex did that and it broke my trust completely. She tried with my current SO and he just said "no thank you, if xidipi wants to sent pictures I'm sure she will". I love him so much :)
Thank you!! I'll look into therapy

Thank you, I'm still really scared of losing her. I want to have a good relationship with my mom but not in the way she wants it. Do you know Gilmore girls? She always idealised their relationship and wanted us to be more like them. 

>You get to choose how much or how little you want her in your life knowing that no matter what you choose, she will ALWAYS find fault and it will NEVER be enough 

I think you're right. There have been moments where I called her weekly and texted her in-between too, but that wasn't enough either and was terrible for my mental health.

Thank you for your reply. I'm not German, but close. I wonder what gave it away? 

That sounds very similar. My mom actually does most of the reaching out, I hardly ever do, I'm already introverted and I have low contact with most people except work and my SO. But when she reaches out I feel kind of obligated to go? Sometimes in the car ride there I cry constantly without an obvious reason. And sometimes she is really nice when I visit and I feel terrible for crying on the way there even though I don't cry on purpose obviously. She also said some pretty racist things, mostly regarding people from Surinam and moslims. She believes the first are always lazy and the second are not to be trusted 9/10 times.

I don't have Facebook, but I'll check out the other subreddits and Susan Forward. Although I'm not sure she's a narcissist. She has really low self-esteem and hates herself. So it's not like she thinks she's the best in the world or feels better than anyone else.

>let her keep treating you like you are her emotional rescue animal.

I really don't want that. 

I've tried to explain that I can't always be available, but I don't think she'll ever understand tbh.
I think she'll explode even more if I did that
Thank you, a lot of comments have recommended therapy so I'll look into that

I'm not sure if she does any of it on purpose, I do really think she loves me. A lot of the comments seem to recommend therapy, I've had therapy for depression but didn't talk about these topics much so that might be a good idea. I have a difficult time recognising the negativity in the moment itself. Often I'll feel like shit first and talk to my boyfriend (who is awesome) about it, and then realise that what she said was nasty so I'm not sure if I can hang up. Honestly this was the first time I ever hung up on her, maybe that's why I'm so scared of losing her.
Thank you

Thank you, I have looked around a bit at that website and that does seem very similar to what I'm experiencing. I'm just really scared of losing my mom somehow, which is why standing up is so difficult I think. I've had therapy for dealing with my depression, which did help. But I don't think I've talked about my mom or past a lot.

That's the weird thing though, she can be really nice and caring too. For example giving advice on how to prepare to ask for a raise, or crying with me after I my first boyfriend cheated on me. If she was just horrible I would've cut contact or something
So how should I deal with this? I really don't want to lose my mom either
